channel.title: Hattiesburg Hub — Local News & Community Stories
channel.description: Your go-to source for local news, community stories, and everything happening in Hattiesburg, MS.

image.title: Hattiesburg Hub — Local News & Community Stories

item.title: Living History: Sixth Street Museum District Showcases Hattiesburg's Past, Inspires the Future
item.description: The Sixth Street Museum District in Hattiesburg's Mobile/Bouie Neighborhood showcases the city's historic African American center of culture and business, featuring the African American Military History Museum, Eureka School, Smith Drug Company, Oseola McCarty House and the forthcoming Moeller Military Vehicle Museum.
item.author: Joseph Bryant

item.title: Surpassing Expectations: Hattiesburg Zoo Creates Model for Growth, Popularity and Stability
item.description: Now beginning its 76th year of operation, the Hattiesburg Zoo continues to evolve with its exhibits, programs and a financial model — including the Serengeti Springs water park — designed to ensure its success and stability.
item.author: Joseph Bryant

item.title: Traveling Choir Brings Palm Sunday Concert Back to Hattiesburg
item.description: Road Trip Manager Demetrius 'MeMe' Marsalis and the Benjamin Cone III & Worship Choir return to the Pine Belt for their fourth annual Palm Sunday Concert.
item.author: Hailey Lanham, WDAM

item.title: Work Starts on Asbury Hospice House Expansion in Hattiesburg
item.description: A groundbreaking ceremony was held for the Asbury Hospice House expansion, a $3 million project that will add family areas, children's play spaces, a pavilion, and a larger pharmacy.
item.author: Sethanie Smith, WJTV

item.title: Local Businesses Gear Up for HUBFEST Weekend
item.description: After more than three decades, HUBFEST continues to bring big crowds and big business to downtown Hattiesburg, with an estimated 25,000-30,000 people expected and a $1.5 million economic impact.
item.author: WDAM

item.title: Fleetwood Mac Tribute Band to Perform at Hattiesburg's Saenger Theater
item.description: Rumours ATL: A Fleetwood Mac Tribute will bring the sounds of the legendary band to the Saenger Theater in Hattiesburg on October 9, 2026.
item.author: Sethanie Smith, WJTV

item.title: Hattiesburg Native Returns to Hometown on Band's National Tour
item.description: Brandon Miller, lead singer and guitarist for A Foreigner's Journey to Boston, brings his music back to Hattiesburg with a concert at Brewsky's on March 28.
item.author: WDAM

item.title: Southern Miss Routs Troy 12-4 at Pete Taylor Park
item.description: The Golden Eagles improved to 19-5 on the season with a dominant 12-4 victory over the Troy Trojans at Pete Taylor Park in Hattiesburg.
item.author: ESPN

item.title: Mississippi's Dr. Daniel Edney Under Consideration to Lead CDC
item.description: Mississippi State Health Officer Dr. Daniel Edney, a vaccine proponent who has led the state's health department since 2022, is under serious consideration to become the new director of the CDC.
item.author: Nick Judin, MS Free Press

item.title: Mississippi State Baseball Completes Commanding SEC Sweep of Vanderbilt
item.description: The No. 6 Bulldogs swept Vanderbilt for the first time since 2000, capped by a 17-7 run-rule victory, drawing two of the largest on-campus crowds in NCAA history.
item.author: Sam Sklar, Clarion Ledger

item.title: Tatum Park Welcomes Hundreds of Kids for Hattiesburg Diamond Youth Baseball Opener
item.description: Hattiesburg Diamond Youth Baseball kicked off its 2026 season at Tatum Park with more than 350 kids participating across five age-group teams, from Tee-ball to Majors.
item.author: WDAM

item.title: Nighttime Closures on U.S. 49 in Hattiesburg Begin March 23 for Railroad Repairs
item.description: Drivers should prepare for overnight closures on U.S. Highway 49 starting March 23, as Norfolk Southern begins railroad bridge repairs expected to last about a month.
item.author: WDAM

item.title: From Hand-Washing Clothes to Changing Lives: New Hattiesburg Museum Honors Legacy of Oseola McCarty
item.description: Oseola McCarty, a humble washerwoman who saved $280,000 over a lifetime of hand-washing laundry, donated $150,000 to fund scholarships at USM. Her restored home is now Hattiesburg's newest museum.
item.author: Joseph Bryant

item.title: Cheapest Gas Stations in Hattiesburg
item.description: CheapInsurance.com compiled a list of the cheapest gas stations in Hattiesburg, helping local drivers find the best fuel prices across the Hub City.
item.author: Laurel Leader-Call

item.title: Mississippi Could See Tornadoes Sunday and Snow on Monday
item.description: Mississippi faces a wide range of weather conditions including severe storms with possible tornadoes Sunday night and below-freezing temperatures with snow possible in northern parts of the state Monday.
item.author: Brian Broom, Clarion Ledger

item.title: Mississippi House Passes Bill to Bypass ABC Warehouse Amid Alcohol Backlog
item.description: The House passed the 'Emergency Alcohol Distribution Act' in a bipartisan 112-2 vote, allowing licensed permit holders to buy directly from manufacturers for two years while the state's ABC warehouse struggles with a software failure.
item.author: J.T. Mitchell, SuperTalk MS

item.title: One Dead, Thousands Without Power in Mississippi After Storms
item.description: More than 50,000 were left without electricity after storms damaged power lines across Mississippi. One fatality and three injuries were reported in Lawrence County, with another cold front expected to bring freezing temperatures and possible snow.
item.author: Brian Broom, Clarion Ledger

item.title: $6,000 Teacher Pay Raise Gains Mississippi Senate's Approval
item.description: A surprise $6,000 teacher pay raise gained approval in the Mississippi Senate, raising salaries over three years for regular teachers, special education educators, assistant teachers, and college professors.
item.author: Heather Harrison, MS Free Press

item.title: Hattiesburg Pharmacy Owner Pleads Guilty to Tax Offense
item.description: Duke Kimbrell Rodgers, 68, of Rodgers Family Pharmacy pled guilty to failing to remit over $1.5 million in employee tax withholdings to the IRS over seven years, agreeing to pay more than $2 million in restitution.
item.author: Sethanie Smith, WJTV

item.title: What to Expect in Mississippi's State Primaries
item.description: Mississippi voters choose nominees for Congress in a state primary Tuesday. Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith faces a primary challenge, and the entire U.S. House delegation is up for reelection.
item.author: Robert Yoon, Associated Press
